pages.text:
<name> had spent weeks building his robot, Sparky, for the school science fair. It was meant to roll in a straight line, beep at obstacles, and even light up with colorful LEDs. Today, the gym was buzzing with students, parents, and teachers. Projects lined the walls, and the air smelled of glue, paint, and excitement. <name> carefully placed Sparky on the display table, double-checking the circuits.

“Ready for your big moment?” <name> whispered to the robot.

He pressed the start button — and Sparky shot forward like a rocket! Zoom! It darted across the hall, zigzagging between tables, knocking over a tower of colored pencils. “Whoa! No, no, no!” <name> shouted, sprinting after it.

Sparky slid under the refreshment table, sending juice boxes flying like tiny missiles. Students ducked, parents laughed, and teachers tried not to slip on spilled lemonade. Aarav, <name>’s best friend, ran alongside him, grabbing stray pencils and shouting, “Catch it before it bumps into the cookie display!”

The robot made a sharp turn and nearly tumbled into the prize-winning volcano experiment, where red foam bubbled over the edges. <name> dove, barely avoiding a sticky mess. “It’s like chasing a hyper puppy on a sugar rush!” he laughed, heart pounding.

Sparky skidded across the gym, bouncing off a stack of science magazines, then spun wildly near the robotics club table. Tiny robots, toy cars, and a floating drone scattered in its wake. “Hang on, Sparky!” <name> yelled, lunging, but the robot slipped past him again.

Finally, Sparky climbed partway onto the stage, tangled in streamers from a previous event. <name> carefully tiptoed, grabbed a chair for leverage, and reached for the robot. But a sudden sneeze from a nearby student startled him — and Sparky wriggled free again, spinning toward a corner filled with art projects. Paint jars teetered dangerously.

Thinking fast, <name> remembered the manual override button on the remote. “Come on, Sparky, stay still!” he whispered. With a quick press, the robot froze mid-beep, its LED lights blinking steadily. <name> breathed a sigh of relief and tightened a loose wire to make sure Sparky wouldn’t move again.

The gym fell silent for a moment — then erupted into cheers and applause. Friends clapped, parents laughed, and teachers smiled. <name> lifted Sparky high. “He’s behaving now!” he said with a triumphant grin.

During the demonstration, Sparky rolled perfectly, dodged tiny obstacles, and even beeped in rhythm with the music. Students crowded around, asking questions, while <name> explained how he built the circuits and coded the movements. He laughed, remembering the chaos from just minutes ago — the flying pencils, the skidding juice boxes, and the near-disaster with the volcano foam.

By the end of the fair, judges awarded <name> a special prize for creativity and problem-solving. “You didn’t just build a robot,” one judge said, “you showed quick thinking and teamwork under pressure.” Aarav nudged him and grinned, “Next time, we should code a seatbelt for Sparky!” <name> laughed, imagining the little robot safely rolling everywhere without causing mayhem.

Walking home with Sparky in his backpack, <name> felt proud. He had faced chaos, thought fast, and saved the day, all while keeping his sense of humor. The robot was finally behaving, and he couldn’t wait to add even more fun features — maybe a confetti cannon next!

That night, <name> set Sparky on the desk, smiling at the blinking LEDs. “You and I make a great team,” he whispered. Even though the robot had caused a hilarious mess, it had taught him something important: sometimes, the most memorable adventures come from the unexpected moments.
